Action Plan:
1. Start oral anti-inflammatory therapy: advise ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily with food; stop if heartburn develops. (Dose/frequency documented by clinician.)
2. Arrange blood tests: send blood-test request form to patient's home for a "full screen" including inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, and evaluation for gout; patient to attend a phlebotomy site per instructions. Expect results in ~5–6 days after sampling.
3. Follow-up review after blood tests: clinician to review results and examine joint; follow-up may be telephone, video, or face-to-face per patient preference — patient to contact clinic after blood tests or sooner if needed.
4. Safety-netting / urgent advice: seek urgent assessment (phone/video or in-person) if the elbow becomes very red, very painful, if redness spreads, or if systemic symptoms develop — this would require immediate evaluation for possible infection.
5. Administrative: clinician will send forms and arrange follow-up logistics.
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Noticed swelling at the tip of the left elbow for ~1 week (noticed in shower).
  - Describes it as not painful or only a bit "weird"; feels slightly warm and fluid-like.
  - Full range of motion preserved; no functional limitation.
  - No known antecedent trauma or injections.
- Onset / course:
  - Began approximately one week ago; feels slightly better since initial notice.
- Past medical history:
  - Osteoarthritis diagnosed by GP a few years ago.
  - Otherwise reports being generally fit and well.
- Medications:
  - No regular medications reported.
- Social history:
  - Desk-based job (sits at a desk).
  - Exercises: runs 2–3 times/week.
- Allergies:
  - Peanuts (food allergy).
  - No drug allergies reported.
- Family history:
  - Patient unsure; no known family rheumatologic disease reported.

Objective:
- Local examination (documented by clinician during video/visual exam):
  - Visible swelling localized to the tip/olecranon of the left elbow.
  - Skin over the tip slightly dry.
  - Area slightly warmer than adjacent skin.
  - Tip of elbow itself tolerates palpation; adjacent swelling area mildly uncomfortable but not markedly tender.
  - Full range of motion of the elbow preserved.
- Systemic:
  - No systemic symptoms documented (no fever, no malaise).
- Investigations:
  - No labs/imaging performed yet.
  - Plan documented to perform blood tests (see Action Plan).

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left olecranon bursitis:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Aseptic (non-septic) olecranon bursitis. (DDx: "Aseptic (non-septic) olecranon bursitis" — High likelihood.)
   - Differential diagnosis (from DDx, consistent with transcript):
     - Septic olecranon bursitis / localized cellulitis — Medium likelihood.
       - Supporting: local warmth and swelling may indicate infection.
       - Opposing: minimal pain, no systemic features, clinician felt it did not appear septic at present.
     - Gout-related bursitis / crystal arthropathy — Medium likelihood.
       - Supporting: acute localized swelling and warmth; clinician plans gout testing.
       - Opposing: patient reports minimal pain; no known prior gout history.
     - Benign soft-tissue mass (lipoma / synovial cyst) — Low likelihood.
       - Opposing: acute onset and warmth favor inflammatory causes over chronic benign mass.
     - Traumatic/hematoma from unnoticed minor injury or repetitive microtrauma — Low likelihood.
       - Opposing: patient denies trauma and no bruising noted.
   - Investigations planned:
     - Blood tests: inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibody panel, and tests to assess for gout (forms to be mailed; patient to attend for phlebotomy).
   - Treatment planned:
     - Start ibuprofen 400 mg PO twice daily with food; stop if heartburn occurs.
     - Conservative monitoring; no aspiration or antibiotics initiated at this time.
   - Referrals:
     - None documented. Follow-up arranged with GP clinic for review of results and reassessment; escalation if concerns for infection.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vital signs documented (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure).
  - No baseline laboratory values available yet (tests planned).
  - No imaging or aspiration performed — none documented or ordered in the transcript.
  - No documentation of duration/timing for follow-up appointment (patient instructed to contact after tests).
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None identified — DDx aligns with clinician assessment of bursitis and includes septic and gout possibilities; no direct contradictions. (If any conflict had existed it would be marked "conflict noted.")
- Transcript quality:
  - Conversation audible and coherent; no significant background noise or unintelligible segments that affected clinical content.
